panels.title: Frontend availability
panels.description: Successful frontend calls as a percentage. Mirrors the availability panel in temporalio/dashboards.

panels.title: Persistence availability
panels.description: Successful persistence calls as a percentage. Drops here precede everything else going wrong.

panels.title: Actions/sec
panels.description: Billable Temporal Actions per second, as the server counts them.

panels.title: Frontend requests/sec
panels.description: All gRPC calls into the frontend.

panels.title: Frontend p95 latency
panels.description: 95th percentile frontend handler latency.

panels.title: Persistence ops/sec
panels.description: Database operations per second across all four services.

panels.title: Frontend availability over time
panels.description: Watch this during the Worker restart drill: the client-side churn should not dent it.

panels.title: Persistence availability over time
panels.description: Postgres is memory-capped in this stack, so sustained load shows up here first.

panels.title: Request rate by service
panels.description: frontend, history, matching and worker all run in the one auto-setup container.

panels.title: Frontend request rate by operation
panels.description: RecordActivityTaskHeartbeat should lead: this demo heartbeats once per item.

panels.title: External events/sec
panels.description: Client-initiated Workflow traffic. Should track the load generator's achieved start rate.

panels.title: Errors/sec by type
panels.description: serviceerror_NotFound and serviceerror_Canceled are routine; serviceerror_ResourceExhausted means the server is shedding load.

panels.title: Errors/sec by operation ($service)
panels.description: Scoped by the Service picker at the top of the dashboard.

panels.title: Frontend latency percentiles
panels.description: Frontend handler latency. Excludes time the caller spent long-polling.

panels.title: Service latency p95 by operation ($service)
panels.description: Per-operation p95 for the selected services.

panels.title: Requests vs errors ($service)
panels.description: Absolute volumes behind the availability stat.

panels.title: Workflow task traffic
panels.description: The add/start/respond triple should stay balanced; a gap means tasks are timing out.

panels.title: Activity task traffic
panels.description: Heartbeat volume is the server-side cost of this pattern. Lowering HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS raises it.

panels.title: Workflow completions/sec
panels.description: Server-side completion stats. The failure series read zero until the server first emits them.

panels.title: Workflow duration p95
panels.description: Server's own view of Workflow wall time, for cross-checking the SDK and load generator numbers.

panels.title: Activity end-to-end latency p95
panels.description: Schedule to completion across retries, measured by history.

panels.title: Activity attempts and timeouts
panels.description: A schedule-to-start timeout means no Worker claimed the task in time, which is a different failure from the injected chaos.

panels.title: Task schedule-to-start latency p95 by task type
panels.description: The queue-backlog signal. Rising Activity latency here means the Worker is out of slots.

panels.title: Task queue backlog
panels.description: Tasks waiting for a poller, excluding the server's internal system queues.

panels.title: Backlog age
panels.description: Age of the oldest queued task. More actionable than raw count.

panels.title: Poll outcomes/sec
panels.description: A sync match is a task handed straight to a waiting poller without touching the database.

panels.title: Match latency p95: sync vs async
panels.description: Async matches went through persistence, so they cost more.

panels.title: Matching pressure
panels.description: no-poller tasks accumulate when work arrives with nothing polling for it.

panels.title: Persistence requests vs errors
panels.description: Absolute volumes behind the persistence availability stat.

panels.title: Persistence latency p95 by operation
panels.description: UpdateWorkflowExecution usually leads, since every heartbeat checkpoint is a mutable state write.

panels.title: Persistence ops/sec by service
panels.description: history should dominate.

panels.title: Persistence errors/sec by type
panels.description: ShardOwnershipLost is normal during shard movement; timeouts are not.

panels.title: Postgres connection pool
panels.description: in-use pinned to max is connection starvation, and it shows up as persistence latency.

panels.title: Per-shard persistence RPS vs host limit
panels.description: persistence_shard_rps is a histogram of observed per-shard rates, not a gauge. Approaching the host limit is what produces ResourceExhausted errors.

panels.title: State transitions/sec
panels.description: Mutable state transitions, the server's unit of Workflow progress.

panels.title: Shard count and churn
panels.description: NUM_HISTORY_SHARDS is 4 in this stack. Churn should be flat once the server settles.

panels.title: Shard acquisition latency p95
panels.description: Time to take ownership of a history shard.

panels.title: Shard lock latency p95
panels.description: Contention inside a single history shard. Rises before persistence latency does.

panels.title: History queue lag p95
panels.description: How far behind the transfer and timer queues are running.

panels.title: Workflow state size p95
panels.description: Heartbeat details are stored on mutable state, not in history, so a large checkpoint payload lands in the first series.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: Per-role goroutine counts inside the one container.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: The temporal container is memory-capped in compose, so this is worth watching under load.

panels.title: GC pause p95
panels.description: Despite the _ms name the buckets are seconds.

panels.title: Restarts and build age
panels.description: A rising restart count means a service is crash-looping.
